the_problem: A 2023 avian-flu outbreak forced Avícola Chequén (Florida, Biobío, 68 years old, Crovetto family) to cull about 200,000 birds on SAG order, leaving it with no productive capacity and heavy debt while it waited indefinitely for SAG clearance to repopulate.
the_decision: General manager Tomás Mandich Crovetto closed the business in an orderly wind-down of the brand, paying all severance. His reason: 'cuando te encuentras con que debe esperarse indefinidamente hasta recibir el alta del SAG, hay decisiones que no pueden esperar'; restarting 'necesitábamos mínimo $1.000 millones' and neither owners nor banks would fund it without insurance.
the_outcome: Operations ended after 68 years, about 50 workers lost their jobs (about 100 had already been cut in the 2023 adjustment); finiquitos paid in full; it was not a legal bankruptcy. The Agriculture minister disputed his account of SAG delays.
